OD-B05-S04.why: Calypso's lines were hidden behind Odysseus.

takes.what: First take. Calypso and Odysseus stand pressed together at the trees, so the only clear cameras left were overhead, and her lines play partly behind his head and the bow on his back.
takes.next: Re-staged: the two stand a man's height apart, step in only for the axe and apart again, so her lines (6-30 s) are held on her own face.

takes.what: The same scene re-staged with room between them: a mid, an over-the-shoulder past Odysseus and a close on Calypso while she names the trees.

OD-B08-S05.why: The first take held one wide of the wooden horse for 51 seconds.

takes.what: First take. Odysseus was not drawn until he waits inside the horse, so for its first 51 s the camera had nobody to cut to and held one static wide of the horse.
takes.next: Re-staged in Alcinous's hall: the bard sings while Odysseus listens, weeps into his cloak, and the king notices, stops the lyre and asks his name; 12 shots, all legal.

takes.what: The song performed in the hall, with the listener's tears and the king's question; 12 shots legal.

OD-B09-S06.why: The great stone did not read as the giant's doing.

takes.what: First take: the crash of the firewood, the flock driven in, the stone heaved into the door, the milking and the fire, the eye on the men; 10 shots legal.
takes.next: The great stone is now carried into the doorway with the giant's heave (a new engine feature: a set piece carried by a body), and the sealed cave and the milking are lit.

takes.what: The stone travels with the giant's arms into the doorway; the sealed cave and the milking lit.

OD-B09-S08.why: The wine was offered to the back of the giant's head.

takes.what: First take: the cave by firelight, the stake cut and hardened, the lots, the wine, the name; 13 shots legal, exposure checked.
takes.next: Re-shot from 43 s and spliced over the first cut (its sound kept): the giant turns round at his seat to face the men, the wine is offered to his face in a low two-shot, then he drinks.

takes.what: The giant turns to the men and the offer is seen face to face.

OD-B09-S10.why: Cameras ended up inside rams and in black night.

takes.what: First published take with the creature camera (72 s): some frames from inside a ram's body or a face, a night wide almost black.
takes.next: Re-shot: no frame inside a ram or a face, the black night wide refused for a lit mid on the lead ram, the closing wide moved off the fleece.

takes.what: The escape under the rams, every camera outside the animals and every frame exposed.

OD-B10-S02.why: The opening wides showed Odysseus's back.

takes.what: First cut (never published): the opening wides look at Odysseus's back, and a wide of a giant runs on into empty sky before the giant is there.
takes.next: The solver learned two rules: a wide on a man prefers his front, and a shot whose figures are gone becomes a wide on a man who is present. 13 shots legal.

takes.what: Odysseus's front in the opening wides, no wide of a giant not yet drawn.

OD-B10-S04.why: Frames from inside the pig sties and of empty sky.

takes.what: First take: 19 of 20 shots legal, but some frames look out from inside the pig stacks or at empty sky, and Eurylochus reports with his back to us.
takes.next: Re-shot: no frame inside the pig stacks or of empty sky, Eurylochus framed from in front, the swine pens in a wide. The solver now refuses a close on the back of a head and a flat frame.

takes.what: Circe's house, the men turned to swine, Eurylochus's report face to the lens.

OD-B10-S05.why: Two-shots showed one speaker from behind.

takes.what: First cut (under review): some two-shots of Hermes and Odysseus show one of the two from behind.
takes.next: The solver now refuses a two-shot that shows either man of the conversation from behind, and a wide that shows a speaker's back.

takes.what: Hermes meets Odysseus on the path and digs the moly; both faces in the two-shots.

OD-B11-S04.why: His mother looked alive; the embraces had nothing to pass through.

takes.what: First take: the blood, the knowing, the longing, three embraces that close on nothing; but Anticleia is drawn as a solid living figure.
takes.next: Anticleia drawn as a shade (translucent and pale, a new engine feature), and each embrace passes through her before she is a step farther off.

takes.what: The mother as a shade, his arms closing through her three times.

OD-B11-S07.why: Achilles never said the line the scene is famous for.

takes.what: First take (62 s): the shades, the praise, the son, the stride across the asphodel, Ajax silent; but Achilles's answer is missing, and the dead look like the living.
takes.next: His answer added as a new turn and spoken on a close of his face (rather a hired man alive than king over all the dead); the four shades drawn translucent and pale; Patroclus and Antilochus bareheaded. 74 s, 14 shots.

takes.what: Achilles answers on his own close, among pale shades.

OD-B13-S01.why: A travelling camera went into a rock.

takes.what: First cut (under review): a camera travelling with a walking man passes into the rock he walks by.
takes.next: The solver now tests a shot's camera every 1.25 s along its move, not only at its start, so a travelling camera stays out of the rock.

takes.what: The tale finished, the gifts, the evening boarding; 6 shots legal.

OD-B17-S03.why: The dog's close-up was of his dark flank.

takes.what: First cut (never published): the dog's close-up from behind his dark flank, his death looked down on from the rafters.
takes.next: The dog's face to the lens, his death at a man's height. The solver: a small beast lying down is seen from a man's height, and an insert on a beast needs its face.

takes.what: Argos on the dung heap, his face, the hidden tear, his death; 5 shots legal.

OD-B17-S05.why: The beggar's retort was cut and the stool was never seen flying.

takes.what: First take (56 s): the begging, the railing, the stool, the blow taken standing, the curse, the rebuke; the beggar's retort is missing and the stool jumps to his shoulder.
takes.next: The beggar's retort restored to the cut and shot, and the stool seen in the air on its arc to his shoulder (a new engine feature: props in flight). 72 s, 16 shots.

takes.what: The retort spoken, the stool thrown and seen on its arc.

OD-B21-S03.why: Eurymachus's shame was not on his face; the bow was bent wrongly.

takes.what: First take (54 s): Leiodes tries first, the suitors one after another, the fire and the tallow, Eurymachus's shame, Apollo's day.
takes.next: Eurymachus says the shame on a close (an added turn), the bow held across the body to bend it, a stray second bow hidden. 58 s, 13 shots.

takes.what: The suitors fail the bow, Eurymachus's shame on his own close.

OD-B21-S07.why: The suitors' reaction was framed from outside the hall.

takes.what: First cut (never published): the suitors' reaction framed from outside the hall, and Odysseus's back while he speaks.
takes.next: The suitors' reaction framed inside the hall. The solver: a close on one of a crowd keeps only his neighbours, a wide weighs a man's front more, no cut back to the shot before last.

takes.what: The string plucked, the thunder, the arrow through the axes; 11 shots legal.

OD-B23-S04.why: A blank wall, speakers from behind, then the back of Penelope's head.

takes.what: First cut (never published): a frame of a blank wall and the speakers seen from behind.
takes.next: No blank-wall frame (a shot with no legal camera had skipped the exposure check) and Penelope's plea with both faces.

takes.what: Second take: 6 shots legal, but the last embrace holds the back of Penelope's head.
takes.next: The last embrace re-shot from above the bed with both of them in frame, rendered as a span and spliced in.

takes.what: The bed test, the recognition, her plea and the long embrace with both faces.
